comment: The one definition of what looks like a secret in text read off the screen, for every platform's helper (ADR-DESK-046).

Each redactor looks at the whole text as read, never at what another left of it, so their order does not matter (owner, 2026-10-08): everything any match takes goes, and one {placeholder} stands for each run of matches that overlap or meet. A match takes itself without what `replacement` copies around {placeholder} at the match's ends; {placeholder} is `placeholder` and $1, $2 are the pattern's groups.
Patterns use the pinned Rust fancy-regex engine on every platform. Native adapters never interpret them. Keep patterns linear on hostile text; the Rust conformance and timing tests are authoritative.
ignoreCase is the only definition flag. Rust compiles this canonical file directly; every platform must pass redaction-cases.json through the linked Rust library.

Every pattern must take time in proportion to the text, whatever the text: no repeat that is scanned again from every position (bound it, or begin the pattern where a run begins). The tests time each on hostile text.

The generator and native regex engines have been retired. Changes must pass the Rust long-continuation, actual-engine-failure and hostile-text timing gates; do not rely on engine-specific pattern rewrites without evidence.

No redactor can hide a secret from another: each finds its secret in the text as read. private-key-cut takes the words of base64 after a header that is cut off, which may hold a later secret's name (the `password` of `password = ...`); that secret's own redactor still finds its value. private-key-body starts only at the start of the text, so that a text starting part-way through a key's line loses that part too.

A key with a distinctive prefix (AKIA, AIza, ghp_, github_pat_, glpat-, xoxb-, npm_, hf_, whsec_, eyJ, sk_live_) goes wherever it is, even glued to the letters before or after it, as the screen shows a key run into a word or a piece of styling. A pattern whose prefix ordinary words also hold keeps the edge before it, each forced by a near miss in redaction-cases.json: sk- (risk-...), Bearer (pallbearer), the _test_ payment keys (benchmark_test_..., task_test_...).

redactors.name: private-key-block
redactors.description: A whole private-key block, from its header to its end line.

redactors.name: private-key-cut
redactors.description: A private-key block cut off where the window ends: its header and the words of base64 after it, each ending at a space, a line break or the end of the text (a word that runs into other characters, such as the `token` of `token: ...` or the `sk` of a key, stays for its own redactor).

redactors.name: private-key-end
redactors.description: A private key's body whose header is not in the text, wherever it is (a page read from the middle of a printed key, after a page number or a running header; a header in a font the reader could not draw, a label beside its first full line): the lines of base64 just before its end line, and the end line.

redactors.name: private-key-body
redactors.description: A text that starts inside a private key's body, its header cut off before the text (a page read from the middle of a printed key, a window scrolled past the header): two or more full lines of base64 at the very start, up to the end line if there is one.

redactors.name: private-key-lines
redactors.description: A private key's body wherever it is, whatever is around it (a page of a printed key between a running header and a footer, several pages of one read together, a label beside its first line; lines ended by \n, \r, U+2028 or U+2029): two or more full lines of base64 one after another, a shorter line between them, and its last, shorter line. A shorter line goes only when it is a whole line that looks like base64 (a digit, + or /, padding, or a small letter before a capital), so a word on its own line after the key (end, Done) stays. Its end line goes with private-key-end. Other runs of such lines (a list of hashes, a base64 blob) go too (owner, 2026-10-05: "redact key bodies anywhere"); one such line alone stays.

redactors.name: json-web-token
redactors.description: A JSON web token: three base64url parts, the first two JSON objects.

redactors.name: bearer-token
redactors.description: "Bearer <token>", as an Authorization header has it. The word stays.

redactors.name: address-password
redactors.description: The password in an address (scheme://user:password@host). The rest stays.

redactors.name: named-value
redactors.description: A value given to a name that says it is secret (password=, api_key:, "token": "…"). The name stays. Only a value with a digit and at least 6 characters, so that "Password: required" stays.
